name: Constraint Inversion via Pairwise Mutual Exclusion
description: I replaced the global "use every resource exactly once" exact-cover constraint with a local pairwise constraint: "select exactly W items such that no two share the same resource". Mathematically, selecting W items from W possible values with no collisions forces a bijection (exact cover), but phrasing it as pairwise mutual exclusion pushes LLMs to model the problem as Maximum Clique or Independent Set on a conflict graph. Because standard clique algorithms scale poorly on dense graphs without exploiting the specific multipartite structure, this reframing is expected to induce TLE or suboptimal search strategies from models relying on surface-level pattern matching.
